description: Solo participant with a background in software engineering, artificial intelligence, and full-stack development. I’m working on a geospatial solution using NASA Earth, Moon, and Mars data to identify terrestrial locations that are similar to lunar and Martian environments.
summary:
TerraAnalog is a web app on a 3D globe that finds the places on Earth most like a chosen Moon base site or Mars site, and explains how they match and where the analogy breaks.

Today, analog sites such as the Atacama Desert or Death Valley are often chosen by reputation. TerraAnalog compares all 339,095 land cells on Earth (0.25° grid, about 28 km) with 15 sites: the Artemis III candidate regions near the lunar south pole, a lunar pit, and seven Mars sites such as Jezero crater. Each place is scored on eight dimensions: terrain, landing and mobility, temperature, light, water ice, rock, barren ground and caves, using NASA open data (LRO, MOLA, MODIS, EMIT, MERRA-2, PDS) and other agency data.

Users pick a site and a purpose (crew training, regolith tests, search for life, base building or caves) and get the top 10 Earth regions, the best spot to test, a 500 m terrain check, NASA EMIT minerals, and an AI assistant that answers only from the data. Results are validated against known analogs: for Jezero, known analog places rank in the top 2.5% of Earth's land, and the best match is the Namib Desert.

It helps mission teams and scientists choose where to test rovers, tools and crews, faster and with evidence.
details:
What it does

TerraAnalog ranks every land place on Earth by how closely it matches a chosen Moon base site or Mars site. Pick a site and a purpose (crew training, regolith tests, search for life, base building, caves, or all dimensions). The app shows the top 10 Earth regions on a 3D globe, colours all of Earth by similarity (top 1%, 10%, 25%), and opens a profile for any place.

How it works

Moon, Mars and Earth data are put on the same 0.25° grid. Each site gets a profile on eight dimensions: terrain, landing and mobility, temperature, light, water ice, rock, barren ground and caves. Every Earth cell gets a score and a closeness word for each dimension, and a purpose averages only the dimensions it needs. For the top regions the app adds a 500 m terrain check, the best spot to test, and NASA EMIT minerals for Mars deserts.

Honest by design

Every profile shows where the analogy breaks (for example, no place on Earth is as cold as the lunar poles). Results are tested against known analog sites: for Jezero crater, known analogs rank in the top 2.5% of Earth's land. When a test does not pass, the app says "Not shown yet".

Benefits and impact

Mission teams and scientists can find new test sites with evidence instead of reputation, and see the trade-offs before they travel.

Tools

Python, FastAPI, xarray, React, globe.gl (3D globe), Docker, pytest and Playwright. The Ask AI assistant uses an OpenAI model and answers only from TerraAnalog's data.

Creativity

One app, two worlds: the same method works for the Moon and Mars, and it explains the "why", not just a score.
